messages:
maya: ran a quick profiling sweep on staging after the canary. seeing host-side overhead spike on short chats (avg tokens 40)
maya: flame shows ~11-13% on grpc read syscall + ~9% in tokenization hot paths (host preproc)
maya: also noticed kvcache churn when seq_len > 1024 — KV eviction noise aligns with small-write bursts from the ingress
maya: paste the tail of the flame and the perf counters:
```
GRPC sys_read  11.8%
host_tokenize 9.4%
writev_coalesce_misses 5.6%
kvcache_evictions 4.9% (spike when seq>1024)
mini-batcher spin 3.1%
```
ryan: hmm. that grpc read % feels high for such short payloads. are we seeing a lot of tiny frames?
ashley: we recently lowered http2 frame size for flow reasons — could be causing more syscalls per request
sam: can you repro with a single client that simulates the short-chat distribution? i can run microbench with 10k reqs
maya: repro script attached (run_local.sh) — it nets the same numbers. also tried enabling prefix cache, still see kvcache thrash when the service silently falls back to the large-req path
leo: two quick ideas: 1) re-enable writev coalescing at the ingress to batch outbound small frames 2) keep a tokenization object pool to avoid repeated allocations during preproc
ryan: agree on pools. also want to try bumping the grpc read window/periodic-read size so kernel doesnt return tiny slices so frequently
ashley: +1 on writev coalesce. the change should be low risk, we have tests for ordering. i can take it if you want
maya: that'd be great. sam — can you run bench w/ writev coalesce simulated? also try a kvcache tweak: raise in-memory shard threshold to reduce spills for seq_len ~1k
sam: will run two benches: baseline, writev-coalesce, and kv-threshold tweak. will post numbers in ~30m
perf-bot: automated-run: ingress-bench-1749997800 completed: baseline p50=82ms p95=210ms; writev-coalesce p50=74ms p95=170ms; kv-threshold p50=76ms p95=160ms
maya: nice, that looks promising. p95 down ~20-25ms with both changes
leo: curious about tail variability. does enabling writev coalesce add latency for cold connections? need to ensure it doesn't add 1-2ms in p50 while improving p95
ryan: we also should update kernel selection heuristics for small-seq workloads: prefer kernels that spend less time in post-processing and more in contiguous decode, to reduce reshuffle cost
ashley: created PR: inbound/writev-coalesce + small unit tests. link: https://git.redwood/inbound/pr/842
maya: added a mini-pool for tokenizer instances in local patch and tested memory impact — negligible (~3MB per host)
sam: bench results:
- baseline: p50=82ms p95=210ms
- writev-only: p50=79ms p95=178ms
- writev+kv-threshold: p50=76ms p95=160ms
- writev+kv+token-pool: p50=74ms p95=152ms
sam: CPU on host dropped ~6% overall for the synthetic load
leo: can we get a run with the kernel-selection tweak too? i suspect combined will help tail more (reduce kernel-switch stalls)
maya: will instrument kernel-choice timeline next run and dump full flame. putting follow-up on eng-runtime board: ticket ENGRT-1428
ryan: def add an e2e canary matrix: (short chats) x (long chats) x (kv threshold) x (writev on/off) so we don't regress another distribution
ashley: rolling writev-coalesce to canary cluster now (small batch). will monitor tracing and error rates
maya: thanks all — great quick cycle. follow-ups: sam will post full flame + perf counters, leo will prototype kernel-pref hint, ash will watch canary for 1h, ryan will draft e2e canary matrix
ryan: tagging @eng-sre to keep an eye on infra alerts
perf-bot: note: automatic alert on kv-eviction-rate suppressed during canary to avoid noise
maya: closing the thread for now. will reopen if canary shows regressions. :thumbsup:
